title: Lighting in the Workplace as the Visual Environment That Affect the Occupant's Mood: A Literature Review
review_question: To discuss research publications related to the relationship between artificial lighting and mood, specifically its effects on recipients' moods in the workplace.
inclusion_exclusion_criteria: Literature from journals, dissertations, theses, and books from the last 10 years (with some older sources included). Online literature search using keywords: lighting, artificial, visual comfort, mood, office, workplace. Site restrictions: .edu and .ac. File type: pdf.

synthesis_conclusions: The understanding of the non-visual effects of light on the human eye can help ensure psychological health for occupants, even in suboptimal lighting environments.
Appropriate lighting, tailored to worker needs, is crucial for maintaining psychological health in the workplace.
evidence_gaps: More research is needed to evaluate the responses of human subjects to different qualities and quantities of lighting.
Further studies are needed on the effects of illuminance level, CCT, distribution, timing, and duration of lighting on mood.
limitations: The literature review primarily focused on publications from the last 10 years, but occasionally referred to older sources.
The review relied on online literature and specific keywords, potentially limiting the scope of included studies.
